title: Real-Life Dragon Found in Thailand — Named After a TV Dragon!
summary:
Imagine finding a real-life dragon! Well, scientists just did — sort of. They discovered a new species of lizard in the high mountain forests of western Thailand. And guess what? They named it Syrax, after the dragon from the TV show House of the Dragon!

The lizard's scientific name is Acanthosaura syrax. It belongs to a group called mountain horned dragons, which have spiky crests along their necks and backs. This one is special because it's small, has yellowish-green color, and lays lots of eggs — just like the dragon Syrax in the show!

Scientists found it in Mae Wong National Park, high up at more than 1,300 meters. It's so rare that it hasn't been found anywhere else on Earth. That's like discovering a new Pokémon that only lives in one spot!

The researchers used DNA testing to make sure it's a new species. They compared its genes to other lizards and found it's different from all of them. It also has the smallest neck and back spikes of any lizard in its group.

Why does this matter? Because this little dragon might need our help. It only lives in a small area of forest, and if that forest is damaged, the lizard could disappear. Scientists want to protect its home and hope it becomes a "flagship species" — like a mascot for conservation in the area.

So next time you watch House of the Dragon, remember: there's a real-life Syrax out there, and it's a lizard!
why_it_matters: This discovery shows that there are still unknown animals right next to us, and protecting their homes helps keep nature full of surprises.

Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists studying lizards in Thailand.
WHAT: They found a brand-new lizard species and named it Syrax.
WHERE: In the high mountain forests of Mae Wong National Park, more than 1,300 meters up.
WHY: The lizard lives only in this small forest, so scientists want to protect its home before it disappears.
